title: Grove ships complete document scaffolding for Primitives it has never activated, making activation a status flip rather than a build
content:
Three Primitives in this chunk are built out and switched off. The Risk Capital Rental Primitive (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.2.1.1), the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive (.6.3.1.1) and the Core Governance Reward Primitive (.7.1.1.1) each read Global Activation Status: **`Inactive`**, and each carries the complete hub skeleton — three directories, a data repository, failed-invocation and suspended-instance branches, and empty Active/Completed/In Progress containers.

The structure exists before there is anything to put in it. Turning a Primitive on is therefore a status change against pre-existing scaffolding, not an exercise in designing where its records will live.

This is the document-level version of a pattern that recurs in Grove's Instances, where a fully specified allocation is held Active with limits set to zero rather than being deleted. Both trade storage and apparent complexity for activation speed: the deliberative work — what a Primitive's lifecycle looks like, what states exist, where failures go — is done once, in advance, when there is no pressure to move quickly.

Two consequences follow. First, the Artifact's size badly overstates Grove's actual activity: pages of structure correspond to no capital, no counterparty and no operations, so a reader gauging scope by volume will be misled. Second, the `Global Activation Status` field is the only thing standing between an empty scaffold and a live capability, which makes it a high-value line to audit — flipping it commits Grove to a Primitive whose structure was reviewed at a time when nothing was at stake.
